paragraphs.text: Skills page for the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI: inspect, download, upload and edit SKILL.md files
# @dr-co/dsh-skills
A **Skills page** for the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI: a sidebar row that opens a full main panel listi
ng every skill the host knows about — our own, the ones bundled inside installed packages, and the o
nes a plugin provides without any file — with download, upload, rename, enable/disable, and editing
gin provides without any file — with download, upload, rename, enable/disable, and editing built in.
The page reads the filesystem itself instead of asking `ctx.skills` alone, because that service only
reports the skills it can load. A skill whose file is named `_SKILL.md` is invisible to the core on
purpose — and it is exactly the one you need to see when a skill stops working.
## What it does
The list is three sections, each with its own heading, count, and empty state:
| Section | Where it comes from | Colours | Actions |
| **Standard skills in `$DSH_HOME/skills`** | our own directories | green dot when active, grey when
disabled, normal name colour | everything: view, edit, rename, upload, both downloads, enable/disab

le |
| **Skills bundled with plugins** | `<pkg>/skills/*` and `<pkg>/assets/*` of every installed pa
ckage, found through their manifests | pink dot and pink name when active, grey-pink when disabled |

view and both downloads — they live in `node_modules` |
| **Provided by plugins (no file)** | `ctx.
skills.list()` entries with no file on disk | pink, dashed dot | view and `Download SKILL.md`; no ZI
P, because there is no directory to archive |
- **Status** is one 11px dot: green for `SKILL.md`, grey for `_SKILL.md` (ours); pink for an active
packaged skill, grey-pink for a disabled one. A directory holding both files is reported as a confli

ct, in red. The word lives in the dot's tooltip and accessible name, not in the row.
- **Name** take
s every pixel the row has left, with the frontmatter `description` underneath; both are cut with an

ellipsis, never wrapped.
- **Path** is relative to `$DSH_HOME` when it is inside it, otherwise relat
ive to the package; shown in full up to 15 characters and, past that, as its first 7 and last 7 arou
nd three dots (`split/p...ath/foo`). The full path is in the tooltip. Below 640px the column is not

rendered at all and the row keeps the path in its accessible name.
- **View** — the first item in ev
ery row's menu, for all three sections. It opens the same full-page frame as the editor but read-onl
y: the raw text, no `textarea`, no `Save`, a `Read-only` badge, `Close` back to the list, and `Edit`
beside it when the skill may be edited. Nothing is rendered — no markdown, no highlighting — and no
thing can be written from it. A provider skill's text comes from `ctx.skills.get(name)`; if it retur
ns an empty body the page says *content is not available for this skill* rather than showing a blank

the page says *content is not available for this skill* rather than showing a blank screen.
[该节后续省略]
### Colours and themes
Green and grey are the shell's own tokens (`--dsw-alias-state-success-primary` for on, `--dsw-alias-
state-idle-primary` for off), so they match the rest of the interface in every theme for free. Pink
is not in the token set, so the plugin defines two variables of its own and gives both palettes thei
token set, so the plugin defines two variables of its own and gives both palettes their own values:
| Palette | `--dshsk-plugin-accent` | contrast on the panel | `--dshsk-plugin-accent-muted` | contra
lette | `--dshsk-plugin-accent` | contrast on the panel | `--dshsk-plugin-accent-muted` | contrast |
Both clear the 4.5:1 bar for text and the 3:1 bar for the dot, and both are above the shell's green
on white (2.28:1). The dark block keys off `body[data-ds-dark-theme]` — the attribute the shell's ow
n theme presenter writes when it applies a snapshot — and *not* off `prefers-color-scheme`, because
the resolved scheme follows the user's setting (including "system" dark and registered themes), not
the operating system. The test recomputes both ratios from the values in `src/client/styles.js`.
### Two uploads, two contracts
The page button and the row menu are not the same operation, and the difference is deliberate: a str
ay drop should not be able to overwrite a working skill.
[该节后续省略]
## Platform notes (what a plugin cannot do)
Verified against the installed harness (0.2.1-rc.2), not preferences:
- **The sidebar cannot be extended by adding a slot.** The `sidebar` slot is `kind: 'single'` and oc
cupied by the shell's own `SidebarRoot`. The supported extension point is the list slot it declares,
`sidebar.panellist` (`SidebarPanelIconOwnerProps { size, active }`), where the entry's `id` must eq
ual the `main` slot's key (`MainPanelId`). This plugin registers exactly that, plus `ctx.slots.regis
ter({ name: 'main', key: 'dsh-skills', locale: NS }, SkillsPage)` — a real main panel, not a dialog.
Panel switching is the shell's `ctx.layout.selectPanel(id)`. The icon is drawn inline at 24×24, `st
roke="currentColor"`, `stroke-width="1.75"`, `fill="none"`, round joins, and honouring the `size` th

e shell passes.
- **No shared markdown renderer is importable.** The client module table is fixed (`
react`, `react/jsx-runtime`, `react-dom`, `react-dom/client`, `@deepseek-ai/cordis`, `zod`, `@tansta
ck/react-virtual`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-store`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-slots`, `@deepseek-a
i/dsh-client-ui-primitives`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-dockkit`); Shiki and the harness' markdown
component live *inside* the shell bundle and are exported to nobody. Since this version has no previ
ew, the plugin ships no renderer at all — an earlier draft had one of its own for exactly this reaso

n.
- **There is no split-button primitive.** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives` offers `Button`
, a value `SegmentedControl`, and menu surfaces — nothing that is one control with a second action.

The split here is two `<button>` elements in one bordered container with a hairline between them.
-
**A plugin has no build plugin for the bundle wrapper.** The page loads a bundle as a script calling
`window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })`; the harness generates that wrapper with an interna
l tsdown plugin that is not published. `scripts/build-client.mjs` gets the same result with esbuild

plus a small wrapper. The bundle requires only `react`, which the module table does provide.
